speaker: Patient
text: No additional symptoms were reported. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of acute appendicitis does not match your symptoms of jaundice, pruritus, and pale stools; appendicitis typically presents with right lower quadrant pain and fever, not liver dysfunction. Since my earlier request for a Liver Function Panel and Ultrasound has been received, will you be able to provide those results so we can evaluate for biliary obstruction or malignancy? Also, have you noticed any abdominal pain, specifically in the upper right quadrant, or any fever?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cholangiocarcinoma (Bile duct cancer). The combination of painless jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine, combined with a misleading prior diagnosis of appendicitis, strongly suggests an obstructing malignancy in the biliary tree. The requested LFT and Ultrasound results would typically confirm elevated alkaline phosphatase and a mass in the bile ducts.
